subject: Optimize Toolkit — packaging, discount tiers, and technical guidance
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@fastship.ai>
Cc: procurement@fastship.ai
Date: 2027-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Optimize Toolkit — initial proposal and options

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday — enjoyed learning about FastShip.ai's multi-tenant routing use case and the tight 300ms p95 requirement for your live chat agents. Per our conversation, I attached a proposal that outlines three packaging options for the Optimize toolkit (Starter, Scale, and Enterprise) and proposed discount tiers tied to committed monthly tokens + pilot credits.

Quick highlights:
- Starter: short-term pilot credits + access to batching/caching recommendations and a single quantization plan.
- Scale: committed capacity discount, higher KV cache retention, and prioritized model-variant fallbacks.
- Enterprise: SLA-backed throughput, on-prem deployment option, and custom quantization engineering.

Two questions we want to make sure are clear for FastShip: how much of your traffic will be eligible for prefix/KV caching (in % of requests), and how sensitive you are to rare tail latency versus average cost-per-token. Those drive where quantization and batching deliver the best unit economics.

I've attached: Optimizer_Toolkit_Terms_v3.pdf (commercial terms) and a short quant-recommendations workbook (quant-recs.xlsx) with model/latency tradeoffs.

Proposed next step: 30-min call next week to walk the workbook, and I'll bring an infra lead to confirm autoscaling/latency SLO mapping. Are you available Wed or Thu?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: Optimizer_Toolkit_Terms_v3.pdf (pdf, 78KB), quant-recs.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)
From: Maya Patel <maya@fastship.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit — initial proposal and options

Thanks Alex — reviewed quickly with engineering. A few clarifying points before the walkthrough:

1) Caching eligibility: ~60% of our conversational traffic is templated system prompts + order lookup (good candidate for prefix/KV caching). The other 40% is open text.

2) Quantization impact: our concern is quality regression for NER and address normalization. If going to int8 or aggressive 4-bit quant, what guardrails do you recommend for on-production fallback?

3) Commercial: the Scale tier numbers look reasonable but procurement wants to understand how batching affects commit measurement — is commit based on raw tokens consumed or billable tokens after batching/aggregation? That affects forecast reconciliation.

We can do Thu 2:00pm PT for the walkthrough. Also looping in procurement@fastship.ai for any legal/term questions.

— Maya
Head of ML Engineering | FastShip.ai
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T12:08:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: FastShip questions — prep for Thu call

Hannah / Dylan — FYI the FastShip thread. Key asks: caching eligibility ~60%, quantization quality concerns (NER/address), and clarification whether commits measure raw tokens or effective billed tokens after batching.

Proposed concessions to keep competitive:
- Confirm commit measurement: we bill on effective tokens after batching/kv-aggregation (we should be explicit). That usually reduces reported consumption — good for them but reduces revenue — discuss offset with a slightly reduced starter credit but steeper Scale discount.
- Offer a safety net: include a rollback SLA for quantization regressions — 2-week rollback window to previous model variant and 75% credit for impacted calls if regression is detected and validated.
- Technical: recommend a hybrid quant plan — int8 for encoder layers + mixed-precision for decoder logits to preserve NER quality; include 1 week A/B eval in production.

Anything to add before I send the updated terms back to Maya?

Alex
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@fastship.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-12T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit — packaging, discount tiers, and technical guidance

Hi Maya — thanks for the detail and the time on Thu. Per Alex's note, we've updated the proposal to be explicit on billing and added technical guardrails for quantization. Summary of changes (see attached).

Commercial clarifications:
- Commit accounting: commits will be reconciled against billed tokens (post-batching and after KV cache hits). Your monthly committed tokens are measured on the billed tokens after system-level aggregation. This reduces your forecasted consumption and is favorable to you; for clarity we provide a sample reconciliation in the appendix.
- Discounting: new Scale tier increases discount at 250M billed tokens/month and again at 1B. We included an early-adopter bonus credit of 25k tokens for the first three months if you sign a 12-month Scale commit.

Technical guardrails and rollout plan:
- Quantization plan: recommend mixed-precision (8-bit weight quant + fp16 activations where per-layer sensitivity indicates). See quant-recs.xlsx for per-model guidance.
- Safety net: a rollback/quality-monitoring policy — if automated evals on your NER/address prompt set (we'll run your red-team prompt pack) detect >2.5% absolute degradation in F1 for NER or >1.5% MRR increase for address normalization errors, we will trigger an immediate rollback and credit 75% of billed calls impacted during the regression window (max 30 days).
- Pilot A/B: 1 week shadow A/B on 5% traffic, then 2-week canary at 25% before full rollout. We'll provide scripts to collect labeled examples for fast triage.

Attached: Optimizer_Toolkit_Terms_v3.pdf (updated sections highlighted) and quant-recs.xlsx (per-model sensitivity matrix + recommended per-layer quant profile).

Next steps: confirm Thu 2:00pm PT and we'll send an updated calendar invite with agenda (workbook walkthrough + procurement questions).

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Product — Optimize | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Optimizer_Toolkit_Terms_v3.pdf (pdf, 82KB, updated), quant-recs.xlsx (spreadsheet, 30KB, per-model sensitivity)
From: Maya Patel <maya@fastship.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@fastship.ai
Date: 2027-02-16T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit — packaging, discount tiers, and technical guidance

Thanks Hannah — that level of clarity helps a lot. Two quick confirmations before the call:

1) Commit accounting & forecasting — understood and we appreciate the sample reconciliation. Procurement will want the reconciliation spreadsheet attached to the SOW.
2) Rollback SLA & credits — the 75% credit and automated eval thresholds look reasonable. We'll share our NER evaluation pack ahead of the call so you can pre-run the checks.

We are good for Thu 2:00pm PT. I'll have our Head of Procurement and a senior ML engineer on the call.

See you then — Maya
